subject: Residency, retention & transfer — routing evidence and subprocessor handoff
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@paywell.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: security@paywell.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency / retention evidence for upcoming due diligence

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team needs a short packet that explains exactly where request processing happens, which subprocessors touch data, and what guarantees we can expect for retention and deletion across borders. Specific asks from our SOC reviewer:

- A map of regions where inference and storage occur for hosted deployments (preferred: regional hops called out).
- A current list of subprocessors and whether any of them can cause cross-border routing.
- Typical timelines for data TTL and how deletion requests propagate to caches/third parties.
- Any standard contractual language / controls we can point reviewers to (SLA, DPA snippets).

Can you send a concise packet (1–3 pages) and a CSV inventory if possible? We have a procurement call on Wednesday.

Best,
Rajesh
Rajesh Kumar
Head of Security Operations
PayWell

--

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@paywell.com>
Cc: security@paywell.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency / retention evidence for upcoming due diligence

Hi Rajesh —

Appreciate the clear list. I attached a short packet and our current subprocessor CSV (exported today). High-level summary below and answers to your bullet points:

• Regions & routing: Primary inference execution for PayWell (hosted plan) will be routed to the customer-selected region (we currently support us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). When capacity requires, we may fail over to a compatible region in the same geopolitical area. Our attached PDF includes a sequence diagram showing typical in-flight hops and where transient cache/KV entries may be stored.

• Subprocessors: The CSV lists subprocessors, purpose, and region. Most network-facing infra (e.g., CDN, monitoring) is US-based; compute partners for hot inference are in the same cloud region as your selected deployment unless a fallback occurs. We call out any subprocessors that could cause exports (e.g., centralized logging ingestion in us-east).

• Retention & deletion: By default request payloads are retained for 30 days for transient caching and prompt/response telemetry used for quality monitoring (this is configurable under enterprise plans). Deletion requests (subject to DPA workflow) are queued and propagated to runtime caches and our long-term storage within 72 hours; downstream subprocessor erasure depends on the subprocessor SLA — the CSV marks those with 30/90/180-day erasure windows.

• Contractual language: I included DPA excerpts and a link to our standard SLA section that addresses residency commitments and routing fallback behavior. If you need redlines we can pull legal in.

Attachments: redwood_processing_map_20270314.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_2027-03.csv, residency_retention_summary.pdf

If you want, Connor (cc'd) can provide the low-level routing evidence for his team to validate.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Residency / retention evidence for upcoming due diligence

Connor, Marissa — looping you both in to confirm the packet I sent PayWell and to ask for one small addition: their reviewer wants a short note that explicitly states whether any of our listed subprocessors have the ability to initiate cross-border egress (yes/no) and the compensating control (contractual/technical) for each.

Could you:
- Connor: validate the regional hop diagram (attached). Add any missing exec locations where requests may transiently land (edge->regional->control plane).
- Marissa: add a single column to the CSV with "egress_possible" (yes/no) and a 1-line control note for each row. If you can drop the edited CSV back to me today I will send to the prospect.

Thanks — this one is time-boxed, procurement call Wed afternoon.

Irene

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Residency / retention evidence for upcoming due diligence

Irene — quick review done. A couple of notes:

1) Diagram: added us-west-2 and us-east-1 execution lanes and labeled the control-plane-only hops (these never see request payloads). Also called out our caching layer TTL semantics (per-tenant prefix caching, TTL default 24–48 hours).
2) Egress risk: The following components could cause cross-border routing only under capacity fallback: secondary compute pools (same cloud provider, different region) and centralized analytics consumers. Both are controlled via routing policy (region preference, then availability zone, then fallback policy).

I didn't make legal statements — left a placeholder where we need Marissa to confirm egress_possible + control text per subprocessor. Dropped revised PDF back to Irene.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Rajesh / team — attaching the updated CSV with the "egress_possible" column filled and short control notes inline. Summary of changes and clarifications:

- Egress_possible: "no" for storage-only subprocessors confined to the selected region (listed as "no (contract + network ACL)").
- For CDN/edge partners: "yes (fallback only)" with controls: routing policy, IP allowlist, contractual DPA clause requiring regional pinning whenever requested, and a 90-day erasure SLA.
- For centralized analytics: "yes (ingestion pipeline)" noted; we flag that telemetry is pseudonymized prior to export and covered by a processing addendum.

Next steps: Irene to confirm the two small clarifications on TTL windows in the PDF. Once confirmed Irene, send the packet to PayWell and I will upload the CSV to the shared Drive link.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
